name: Rosewood Inn of the Anasazi
positioning: Boutique inn in downtown Santa Fe, opposite the Palace of the Governors, with Southwestern rooms and a restaurant built on local ingredients
best_for: Travelers who want to walk to Santa Fe's historic Plaza
Food and wine lovers drawn to a farm-sourced restaurant and a large wine cellar

facts.text: The hotel is in downtown Santa Fe, opposite the Palace of the Governors and steps from the historic Plaza.
Guestrooms have handcrafted furnishings and traditional wood ceilings.
Accessible rooms have a king-size bed and an intimate sitting area.
The Anasazi Restaurant serves contemporary American cuisine inspired by local ingredients.
The Anasazi Restaurant's dishes are guided by the seasons and sourced from local farms.
The Patio is the hotel's plaza restaurant, set in the heart of downtown.
The hotel offers guests a complimentary car service.
The hotel can arrange in-room massage and aromatherapy.
A guided tasting of premium tequilas is offered, and reservations are required.
A Bespoke Romantic Dinner includes a five-course wine pairing menu.
The name Anasazi refers to the Native American civilization that once inhabited the Four Corners region.

highlights.text: The wine collection numbers over 900 wines, curated by the in-house wine director.
The basement wine cellar doubles as a private dining room that can be reserved for intimate gatherings.
Chef Cristian Pontiggia, a native of Lombardy, was named Chef of the Year in New Mexico 2023 by the New Mexico Restaurant Association.
Custom Anasazi bicycles are available for guest use, with suggested routes including Canyon Road and the Railyard District.

considerations.text: There is no spa or pool on site.
WhataHotel notes limited on-site amenities due to the hotel's boutique size.
